evidence: "Any automated processing of PRs from an external fork is potentially dangerous and such PRs should be treated like untrusted input." TL;DR: pull_request_target + explicit checkout of untrusted PR 'may lead to repository compromise.'
correction: Full title: 'Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 1: Preventing pwn requests', Jaroslav Lobacevski, GitHub Security Lab, 3 Aug 2021.

evidence: Page has Code-Review, Branch-Protection and Dangerous-Workflow sections. Code-Review: "Reviews may also detect or deter an attacker trying to insert malicious code". Dangerous-Workflow: "determines whether the project's GitHub Action workflows has dangerous code patterns."
correction: Living doc on main; cite as accessed 2026-10-21 rather than fixed year 2025.

evidence: Abstract: "the untrusted data retrieved by the LLM can never impact the program flow"; "solving 77% of tasks with provable security (compared to 84% with an undefended system) in AgentDojo."
correction: Debenedetti, Shumailov, Fan, Hayes, Carlini, Fabian, Kern, Shi, Terzis, Tramer; arXiv 2503.18813 (v1 Mar 2025, v2 Jun 2025).

evidence: Sec 4.10.3: "the code agent only interacts with untrusted documentation or code by means of a strictly formatted interface"; 'Dual LLM with strict data formatting' called "the safest design we can consider here." Dual LLM defined Sec 3.1.
correction: Location more precisely Sec 3.1 (Dual LLM) and Sec 4.10.3 (SWE agent case study). Paper also says no single pattern suffices across threat models.

evidence: Abstract: "utilize transformations of an input to provide a reliable and continuous signal of its provenance"; "reduces the attack success rate from greater than 50% to below 2%" with GPT-family models.
correction: Full title: 'Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting', Hines, Lopez, Hall, Zarfati, Zunger, Kiciman, arXiv 2403.14720 (Mar 2024). 'static attacks' is our gloss; abstract says 'in our experiments' with GPT-family models.

evidence: Abstract: "we bypass 12 recent defenses (based on a diverse set of techniques) with attack success rate above 90% for most; importantly, the majority of defenses originally reported near-zero attack success rates."
correction: Full title: 'The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections', Nasr, Carlini, Sitawarin, Schulhoff, Hayes, et al., arXiv 2510.09023 (Oct 2025).

evidence: Mitigation headings include "4. Enforce privilege control and least privilege access", "5. Require human approval for high-risk actions", "6. Segregate and identify external content". Quote on indirect injection present verbatim.
correction: Quote supports definition of indirect injection, not mitigations; for mitigation claim quote the headings 4-6 instead.

evidence: Post (16 Jun 2025) lists "Access to your private data", "Exposure to untrusted content", "The ability to externally communicate"; "an attacker can easily trick it into accessing your private data" and sending it to them.
correction: Full title: 'The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication', Simon Willison.
